names.name: all flats
names.said: Tacked to the end of the order: 'twenty, lemon pepper, all flats.'

etymology.root: all + flats (plural of flat); an order-modifier phrase, mirrored by all drums
etymology.first_attested: 2018, in 2 Chainz's 'Hot Wings': "She just want her 20-piece/ All flats with the lemon pepper" — the earliest dated printing this project can name
etymology.note: *Inference —* the phrase can only exist where a counter holds enough volume to sort, which is why it belongs to high-turnover wing counters and chains rather than to a bar running one case a night.

text.what: An order that refuses half the bird. A wing splits one-for-one into a drumette and a flat, so a kitchen filling an all-flats order has to sell the drumettes to somebody else — which is why the answer is often no, and why the places that say yes charge for it.
text.how: Say it last, after count and flavour, and expect a wait: somebody is picking through a pan. Chains that will do it price it per wing rather than per order. A counter that cannot do it will say 'they come mixed', which is the polite form of no.
